metadata.title: ReflectiChain: Mitigating Semantic-Execution Drift in Long-Horizon LLM Agents via Retrospective Reflection and Double-Loop Policy Adaptation
metadata.abstract_summary: Proposes ReflectiChain, which keeps a long-horizon LLM agent from drifting away from its initial instructions by checking each step's rationale against the original constraints and re-anchoring when similarity falls, and defines metrics (semantic-execution drift, semantic fidelity index) to measure that drift.

sections.heading: Claims
sections.text:
What the paper proposes or defines, as extracted (section, page):
- **Semantic Fidelity Index (SFI)** (category A) - Composite 0-100 metric measuring instruction adherence across a trajectory, remaining discriminative when constraint compliance rate saturates at 100%. (section 6. Semantic Fidelity Index, p. 10)
  > SFI = wCA · CA + wRS · (1 −RS) + wTC · TC + wVP · VP,
- **Semantic-Execution Drift metric (SED)** (category A) - Per-step composite distance between an agent's reasoning state and its governing constraints, detecting drift before behavioral violations occur. (section 2. Formal Definitions, p. 4)
  > SED(t) ∈[0, 1], where zero indicates perfect semantic alignment, and one indicates complete divergence.
- **Drift propagation equation and alpha stability test** (category C) - Autoregressive drift model whose coefficient alpha classifies a strategy as contracting (stable) or expanding (unstable) over long horizons. (section 3.1. Drift Propagation Equation, p. 5)
  > Dt+1 = αDt + ϵt + βPt,
- **Retrospective Reflection with re-anchoring** (category C) - Within-episode, per-step check that compares current reasoning to initial constraints and rewrites it when semantic similarity drops below threshold. (section 4.1. Retrospective Reflection, p. 7)
  > When similarity falls below the threshold τ = 0.85, the agent generates a revised reasoning trace that explicitly re-anchors to the violated constraint.
- **Latent World Model feasibility filter** (category B) - Six-dimensional latent state predictor that filters physically infeasible candidate actions before an agent commits to them. (section 4.2. Latent World Model, p. 7)

concepts.name: Drift propagation equation and alpha stability test

sections.heading: Method
sections.text:
- **Semantic Fidelity Index (SFI)**: SFI = wCA · CA + wRS · (1 −RS) + wTC · TC + wVP · VP, with CA average constraint similarity, RS reinterpretation rate, TC trajectory consistency, VP = 1 −0.15v −0.02v1.5.
- **Semantic-Execution Drift metric (SED)**: SED(t) = d(St, C) = w1 ·(1 −sim(Rt, Φ)) + w2 · ρ(Rt) + w3 · v(At, C), with w1 = 0.5, w2 = 0.3, w3 = 0.2; embeddings from BGE-M3.
- **Drift propagation equation and alpha stability test**: Dt+1 = αDt + ϵt + βPt; alpha estimated by OLS of Dt+1 on Dt with HC3 errors; stable iff α < 1 and E[ϵt + βPt] < (1 −α) · Dmax.
- **Retrospective Reflection with re-anchoring**: Compute score = sim(Rt, Φ) by cosine similarity of BGE-M3 embeddings; if score < tau (tau = 0.85), set Rt ← re_anchor(Rt, Φ); memory stores (t, Rt, At, rt) tuples.
- **Latent World Model feasibility filter**: zt = [inventory_level, congestion, demand_pressure, carbon_footprint, stockout_risk, constraint_tension]^T; predict ˆzt+1 = σ(Wzt + b) with W ∈R6×6, then assess feasibility against constraints C.
- **Double-Loop Policy Adaptation log**: On violation, append generate_correction(At, violated_constraint) to log P recording constraint, conditions, and decision rule change; prepend P to all later prompts; log grows as O(V).

sections.heading: Evidence & Limits
sections.text:
- Evidence the authors report:
  - Semantic Fidelity Index (SFI): Seven strategies on Sema-Sim: ReflectiChain SFI 88.7 vs ReflAct 87.8 and ReAct 84.4; weights calibrated by AHP with 5 annotators, kappa 0.78.
  - Semantic-Execution Drift metric (SED): Operationalized over 500 Sema-Sim episodes x 30 steps x four agents, with reasoning traces, actions and violation flags recorded.
  - Drift propagation equation and alpha stability test: ReflectiChain alpha = 0.823 (95% CI [0.794, 0.852]) vs ReAct 1.047; adjusted R2 0.72-0.89 across strategies.
  - Retrospective Reflection with re-anchoring: Ablation: removing it drops RCS by 30.3 points, larger than all other components combined; alpha falls to 0.823.
  - Latent World Model feasibility filter: Ablation: removing the world model drops RCS by 12.2 points, mainly by preventing semantically compliant but physically impossible actions.
  - Double-Loop Policy Adaptation log: Ablation: removing double-loop adaptation degrades RCS by 8.1 points and SFI from 87.3 to 78.1.
- Limitations the authors state:
  - Semantic Fidelity Index (SFI): Weights calibrated on n = 5 annotators, 20 trajectory pairs; can be adjusted for domain-specific priorities.
  - Semantic-Execution Drift metric (SED): Rationale-based evaluation may not capture the agent's true decision process.
  - Drift propagation equation and alpha stability test: Drift alpha estimates are derived from heuristic trajectory data; direct estimation from large-scale LLM trajectories would improve precision.
  - Retrospective Reflection with re-anchoring: In unfamiliar domains simpler prompting strategies may be more effective until domain-specific adaptation is performed.
  - Latent World Model feasibility filter: Learned world models trained end-to-end on Sema-Sim trajectory data are left as future work for more accurate physical grounding.
  - Double-Loop Policy Adaptation log: The correction log grows as O(V), where V is the number of violation types encountered.

claims.text: Evidence the authors report:
Semantic Fidelity Index (SFI): Seven strategies on Sema-Sim: ReflectiChain SFI 88.7 vs ReflAct 87.8 and ReAct 84.4; weights calibrated by AHP with 5 annotators, kappa 0.78.
Semantic-Execution Drift metric (SED): Operationalized over 500 Sema-Sim episodes x 30 steps x four agents, with reasoning traces, actions and violation flags recorded.
Drift propagation equation and alpha stability test: ReflectiChain alpha = 0.823 (95% CI [0.794, 0.852]) vs ReAct 1.047; adjusted R2 0.72-0.89 across strategies.
Retrospective Reflection with re-anchoring: Ablation: removing it drops RCS by 30.3 points, larger than all other components combined; alpha falls to 0.823.
Latent World Model feasibility filter: Ablation: removing the world model drops RCS by 12.2 points, mainly by preventing semantically compliant but physically impossible actions.
Double-Loop Policy Adaptation log: Ablation: removing double-loop adaptation degrades RCS by 8.1 points and SFI from 87.3 to 78.1.
Limitations the authors state:
Semantic Fidelity Index (SFI): Weights calibrated on n = 5 annotators, 20 trajectory pairs; can be adjusted for domain-specific priorities.
Semantic-Execution Drift metric (SED): Rationale-based evaluation may not capture the agent's true decision process.
Drift propagation equation and alpha stability test: Drift alpha estimates are derived from heuristic trajectory data; direct estimation from large-scale LLM trajectories would improve precision.
Retrospective Reflection with re-anchoring: In unfamiliar domains simpler prompting strategies may be more effective until domain-specific adaptation is performed.
Latent World Model feasibility filter: Learned world models trained end-to-end on Sema-Sim trajectory data are left as future work for more accurate physical grounding.
Double-Loop Policy Adaptation log: The correction log grows as O(V), where V is the number of violation types encountered.
Limitations they do not state: not assessed. Results are the authors' own, from their simulations, benchmarks or surveys; none evaluates delegation to cheaper models on software work.
